reasoning: The September 2012 meeting introduced QE3: an open-ended, outcome-based program of $40 billion per month in agency MBS purchases with no predetermined end date, explicitly conditioned on 'sustained improvement in labor market conditions.' This is a qualitative shift from the prior regime of the time-limited, balance-sheet-neutral Maturity Extension Program (Operation Twist). The forward guidance was also extended and reframed to signal accommodation 'for a considerable time after the economic recovery strengthens,' introducing a new conditional logic. Together, these constitute the launch of a new QE program — a textbook regime shift.
key_quote: The Desk is also directed to begin purchasing agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of about $40 billion per month... If the outlook for the labor market does not improve substantially, the Committee will continue its purchases of agency mortgage-backed securities, undertake additional asset purchases, and employ its other policy tools as appropriate until such improvement is achieved in a context of price stability.
